name: Retirement visa (Non-Immigrant O-A / O-X)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires the applicant to be at least 50 years old, applying at a Thai embassy or consulate abroad.

Requires at least THB 800,000 held in a Thai bank account for at least 2 months before applying and maintained for at least 3 months after receiving the extension (some immigration offices additionally require the balance stay above THB 400,000 year-round), or monthly income of at least THB 65,000, plus mandatory health insurance from an approved Thai insurer.
requirements.fix_path: Deposit and maintain the required THB 800,000 in a Thai bank account per the timing rules, or document qualifying monthly income, and secure approved Thai health insurance.

requirements.blocker_text: The O-X visa grants 5-year validity in exchange for a materially higher financial requirement than the standard O-A -- the specific current figure was not independently confirmed against a primary source in this research pass, and is available only to nationals of a limited list of eligible countries.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm current O-X financial thresholds and nationality eligibility directly with a Thai embassy or consulate.

evidence_required.document: Bank statements showing the required funds held for the applicable period
90-day address reporting to Immigration Bureau once resident

outcome.duration_length: O-A: 1 year, renewable annually; O-X: up to 5 years, renewable

sources.title: Thai Visa Services -- Best Visa for Long Stay in Thailand 2026, describing the O-A/O-X financial-requirement structure and timing rules

notes: STATUS: DRAFT. HONEST SOURCING GAP: no direct fetch of a Thai embassy or Immigration Bureau page was achieved for this route in this research pass; the O-X category's specific current financial threshold and eligible-nationality list in particular were not confirmed with confidence and are modeled hard:false accordingly. STRUCTURAL FINDING: unlike th_ltr_visa's Wealthy Pensioner category (10-year status, tax exemptions, annual-only reporting) and unlike th_thailand_privilege (pure membership fee, no PR pathway), the retirement visa is explicitly identified by multiple sources as 'the correct visa' if a genuine Thai Permanent Residency pathway matters to the applicant -- LTR and Privilege years do not count toward PR at all, but retirement-visa years on Non-O/O-A status can, subject to the general PR eligibility categories documented on th_permanent_residence. leads_to_citizenship is correctly false at this route's own level: Thai naturalisation requires PR status first (5 consecutive years), so citizenship is only reachable via th_permanent_residence as an intermediate step, not directly from a retirement visa -- a two-hop chain rather than a direct route, worth surfacing clearly given how often retirees might assume otherwise.
